review: Independent metadata route and image-aware warmer lifecycle review

scope.method: Production code with in-memory boundaries and deterministic fixtures; fixed-venv pytest with -B and cacheprovider disabled. Separate image-cache concurrency/security review is outside this report's verdict.

route_verdict: PASS for tested routing, expiry, isolation and TLS fail-closed properties in the current snapshot.

properties: Successful fallback routes are scoped to the exact official hostname; an image route does not replace the API host's normal system-direct attempt.
Successful reuse does not extend the DNS expiry; expired preferences are removed before a new request selects a route.
TLS, short-read and redirect failures fail the current request. They do not weaken certificate validation or retry that current request through another route.
A failed preferred address is forgotten by matching hostname and address; an old request failing on IP A cannot revoke a newer preference for IP B.
After a failed preference is forgotten, the next independent request starts with system-direct. Ordinary connection failure may take the bounded GET fallback path.
Cancellation preserves an otherwise healthy preferred route. Non-2xx responses do not establish a new success preference.
HTTPS verifies the original hostname even when connecting to a DoH-derived IP.

warmer_integration.same_interpreter_evidence: portable_runtime.main constructs and starts Host, whose start constructs ImageService, then enters the native owner loop. That owner starts StartupPreloader in the same interpreter. Consequently the module-local WeakSet is visible to the AM6B warmer; this is not a claim of cross-process IPC.
warmer_integration.meaning: An image miss appearing during a running warm task cancels it cooperatively; completing the image request does not revive that task. No file polling or new GUI command was required for this signal.

clear_lifecycle_findings.initial: When bobi_metadata_epoch was absent, clear_all_cache only erased data. A running warmer compared None with None and did not observe cancellation.
A target successfully warmed before clear_tmdb_cache retained its one-hour in-memory cooldown, preventing that target's cleared metadata from being rewarmed.

remaining_finding.finding: The new idle artwork enrichment can call the existing Fanart path. A network failure returns the truthy DEFAULT_FANART dictionary with fanart_added=false. get_fanart_details persists any truthy dictionary for the normal success TTL; a subsequent foreground request therefore reuses the failed empty artwork rather than retrying.
remaining_finding.fixture: Compile the actual get_fanart and get_fanart_details functions, inject an in-memory cache and a session.get that raises OSError, then call the metadata helper once as warm work and again as foreground work.
remaining_finding.recheck: Re-ran only the original production-function in-memory fixture with the fixed .venv-closure interpreter. Both warm and subsequent foreground requests reach the mocked HTTP boundary, and neither failure default is persisted. The foreground still returns failure because this fixture deliberately fails every HTTP attempt; that is expected and is not rewritten as metadata success.
remaining_finding.source_check: get_fanart_details ignores an old explicit fanart_added=false cache record, returns an empty dictionary for cached_only without a fetch, and writes new records only when fanart_added is exactly true and request budget remains.
remaining_finding.disposition: No remaining finding from this bounded route/warm/clear review. No broader baseline, package, deployment or device verification was repeated by this reviewer.

limits: Metadata and optional artwork cancellation is cooperative; this does not prove immediate interruption of an OS DNS/connect or an already blocking library HTTP call.
Pure-memory and local tests do not prove actual poster latency, AM6B resource usage or UI responsiveness.
A successful route test does not validate unrelated image-server admission, token or filesystem security, which belongs to the other assigned reviewer.
